title: Diatonic triads
description: Harmonize the major scale, Roman numerals, function, and the 4–3–2 ladder.

cards.front: What is a diatonic triad?
cards.back: A triad built on a scale degree using only notes of the key. Harmonize by stacking thirds: degree, degree plus two, degree plus four.

cards.front: List the seven diatonic triads of C major with numerals and qualities.
cards.back: I C major. ii Dm. iii Em. IV F. V G. vi Am. vii° Bdim.

cards.front: How do Roman numerals show quality?
cards.back: Uppercase = major, lowercase = minor, ° = diminished. They stay the same in every key: I–IV–V is C F G in C and G C D in G.

cards.front: What quality pattern appears in every major key?
cards.back: M m m M M m dim — three major (I IV V), three minor (ii iii vi), one diminished (vii°).

cards.front: Why are some stacked thirds major and some minor in a major key?
cards.back: The scale’s half steps shrink the thirds that span them. In C: E–F and B–C. Thirds containing a half step are minor.

cards.front: In C major, which thirds are minor? Which are major?
cards.back: Minor: D–F, E–G, A–C, B–D. Major: C–E, F–A, G–B. Two minor thirds in a row (B–D, D–F) make vii°.

cards.front: How must you spell diatonic chords — from a fixed chord, or from the key?
cards.back: From the key signature. In G major, vii° is F♯ A C, not F A C.

cards.front: Write I through vii° in G, D, and A major.
cards.back: G: G Am Bm C D Em F♯dim. D: D Em F♯m G A Bm C♯dim. A: A Bm C♯m D E F♯m G♯dim.

cards.front: Write I through vii° in F and B♭ major.
cards.back: F: F Gm Am B♭ C Dm Edim. B♭: B♭ Cm Dm E♭ F Gm Adim.

cards.front: Harmonize A natural minor with numerals.
cards.back: i Am, ii° Bdim, III C, iv Dm, v Em, VI F, VII G. Same seven chords as C major, numbered from A.

cards.front: In natural minor, what quality is degree 5? What happens with a raised 7?
cards.back: Natural v is minor. Raised 7 (harmonic minor) makes it major V or V7.

cards.front: Group I, ii, iii, IV, V, vi, vii° by function.
cards.back: Tonic (rest): I, with vi and sometimes iii as substitutes. Predominant: IV and ii. Dominant: V and vii°.

cards.front: Which are the primary triads, and what do they contain together?
cards.back: I, IV, and V. Together they contain every note of the major scale. In C: C E G, F A C, G B D.

cards.front: Why does vii° pull toward I?
cards.back: It contains the leading tone and the 4, which form a tritone. In C: B→C and F→E. It behaves like V7 without a root.

cards.front: On 4–3–2, what fret recipes are major, minor, and diminished from bass fret r?
cards.back: Major r, r−1, r−2. Minor r, r−2, r−2. Diminished r, r−2, r−3.

cards.front: Give the C major ladder on 4–3–2 from F upward (chord, numeral, frets).
cards.back: F IV 3 2 1. G V 5 4 3. Am vi 7 5 5. Bdim vii° 9 7 6. C I 10 9 8. Dm ii 12 10 10. Em iii 14 12 12.

cards.front: How do you build the ladder in any key on string 4?
cards.back: Find the seven scale roots on string 4, then apply the quality pattern for each numeral.

cards.front: G major ladder on 4–3–2 from roots 5 7 9 10 12 14 16. Give the shapes.
What is iii in A major? V in E? IV in B♭? vi in G?
cards.back: C♯m, B, E♭, Em.

cards.front: C – Am – F – G as numerals, then in G and in D.
cards.back: I vi IV V. In G: G Em C D. In D: D Bm G A.

cards.front: Harmonize D major and E major.
cards.back: D Em F♯m G A Bm C♯dim. E F♯m G♯m A B C♯m D♯dim.

cards.front: Harmonize D natural minor.
cards.back: Dm Edim F Gm Am B♭ C as i ii° III iv v VI VII.
